title: introduce-operator-scope-assertion-and-region-obfuscated-audit-writer
author: Priya Menon
description:
Motivation: Customers and internal SOC reviews called out two gaps for high-assurance tenants: (1) operators and runbooks must be constrained to region-scoped duties (operator cannot act outside their assigned region), and (2) audit records stored for some jurisdictions require PII-obfuscation before leaving the region. This PR implements a policy-level 'operator.scope' assertion for RBAC v2 and a pluggable audit obfuscation writer that applies region-aware masks and removes sensitive fields when required.

What this changes: Implements an attribute-driven entitlement check and audit middleware. Key components: 
- rbac/attribute_assertor.go: new attribute evaluator that checks the caller's operator.scope claim (e.g., "eu-west-1", "us-east-1") against resource locality/route annotations. Supports wildcard scopes ("eu-*") and timebound assertions. 
- authz/policy_compiler.v2: small extension to policy DSL to declare 'operator_scope' enforcement points. Compiler emits an extra decision hook when policies include 'scope: region-bound'. 
- audit/obfuscator/region_policy.yaml: declarative rules for per-region fields to obfuscate (email, phone, ssi, raw_prompt). Rules are overridable by tenant flags. 
- audit/writers/obfuscating_writer.go: middleware writer that inspects request metadata (tenant region, kms_key_location) and applies the obfuscation pipeline before handing logs to the storage backend. Supports streaming and batch modes used by the hosted ingestion path. 
- kms/residency_enforcer.go: lightweight check that ensures the CMK referenced in request headers matches the tenant region assertion before allowing write operations; integrates with attribute_assertor and returns structured audit annotations on mismatch. 
- tests/*: unit and integration tests covering assertion evaluation, wildcard matching, obfuscation rules, and failure modes (deny + audit annotation). 

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind 'operator_scope_enforcement' and 'region_audit_obfuscation' runtime flags. Default off for existing tenants. Gradual rollout: enable for internal test tenants, then pilot with 3 EU customers for 2 weeks, followed by org-wide opt-in for tenants with data_residency requirement. 

Backward compatibility and migration: The policy DSL extension is additive; policies without 'scope:' behave as before. Existing audit writers remain available; this PR wires the obfuscating writer as an option behind the feature flag. Derived audit indices and downstream pipelines must be verified by the observability team before wide rollout. 

Testing notes: Ran the internal compliance harness (SEC-211) and the region end-to-end suite. Simulated operator tokens with differing operator.scope claims and verified expected allow/deny decisions and annotated audit entries. Performed a failure-mode test where KMS region mismatches are logged as 'kms_residency_violation' with masking applied and the write rejected. 

Security considerations: Obfuscation uses deterministic hashing for identity fields with tenant-specific salt stored in KMS-protected secret. Never stores raw PII in long-term logs for protected regions. The enforcement path returns structured audit metadata (non-PII) for debugging in the control plane. 

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for attribute_assertor and obfuscating_writer 
- [x] Integration test for KMS residency enforcement 
- [x] Feature flags added and documented in ops/flags.md 
- [x] Release note drafted for compliance channel 
- [x] Reviewed by security and privacy teams

Commits summary: 
- feat(rbac): add operator.scope attribute evaluator and tests 
- feat(audit): add obfuscating writer and region policy config 
- feat(kms): residency enforcer sync with attribute_assertor 
- docs: ops flags and rollout notes 
- test: e2e for region-bound operator flows

Changed files (high level): 
- rbac/attribute_assertor.go 
- authz/policy_compiler.go 
- audit/writers/obfuscating_writer.go 
- audit/obfuscator/region_policy.yaml 
- kms/residency_enforcer.go 
- ops/flags.md 
- pkg/telemetry/audit_annotations.go 
- tests/rbac/operator_scope_test.go 
- tests/audit/obfuscation_integration_test.go 

Related work: This complements ENG-2982 (policy instrumentation) and reuses the key-claim wiring from ENG-2711. It is a smaller-surface alternative to earlier geo-fencing proposals, focusing on operator-scoped assertions rather than global routing changes.

Release notes: Adds operator-scoped RBAC v2 assertions and an optional region-aware audit obfuscation writer. Feature is off by default and must be enabled via runtime flags. See compliance/notes/region-obfuscation.md for tenant onboarding steps.
review_conversation: Daniel Cho (reviewer): Please add a unit test for wildcard scope matching (e.g., 'eu-*'). Also can we avoid blocking writes when obfuscation fails? Maybe fallback to sanitized copy?

Priya Menon (author): Added wildcard tests in tests/rbac/operator_scope_test.go. For obfuscation failures we log an audit_annotation and reject the write for protected regions; added comment explaining this is required by policy (privacy-first), but the behavior is behind a flag and can be relaxed in emergency by ops.

María González (reviewer): KMS residency check looks good — please ensure the error code maps to our existing 'policy.violation' metric for alerts. Also add a short note in ops/flags.md about the pilot tenants.
Priya Menon (author): Added metrics emit (policy.violation.kms_residency) and pilot tenant list to ops/flags.md.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash; PR contained a small fixup commit to align lint rules and an added test for wildcard matching.
release_notes: Adds operator-scoped RBAC v2 assertions and an optional region-aware audit obfuscation writer. Off by default; enable via operator_scope_enforcement and region_audit_obfuscation flags. Pilot with EU tenants before org-wide opt-in.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flags per environment; update log retention/export rules for obfuscated indices. Ensure tenant salts are provisioned via KMS before enabling. See compliance/notes/region-obfuscation.md.
